structure_creation.description: How to create a Structure object

parameters.lattice: Lattice object defining the unit cell
parameters.species: List of element symbols or Species objects
parameters.coords: List of fractional coordinates (default) or cartesian
parameters.coords_are_cartesian: Set True for cartesian coordinates (default: False)

notes: coords can be fractional (default) or cartesian

from_parameters.pattern: Lattice.from_parameters(a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma)

notes: Modifies the structure in place by default; copy it first to retain the reference.
For an integer nonsingular matrix S, the new atom count is N0 * abs(det(S)); nx*ny*nz is the diagonal case.
Use the task-specified input cell and scaling matrix; a conventional cell is not always orthogonal.

parameters.indices: List of site indices to remove (0-based)

notes: Pass all zero-based indices from the current structure in one call.
For separate deletion calls, process original indices in descending order or recompute them after each deletion.

parameters.new_species: New element symbol or Species object

notes: new_species can be string like 'Ga' or Element object
site_replacement.example: structure.replace(0, 'Ge')  # Replace first atom with Ge

add_site.description: How to add atoms to structure
notes: Use coords_are_cartesian=True for Cartesian positions in Angstrom.
Place an adsorbate relative to its local binding site and surface normal in one consistent periodic image.

get_distance.returns: Distance between sites i and j

slab_generation.description: Generate surface slab from bulk structure

parameters.center_slab: True to center slab in cell
parameters.in_unit_planes: If True, min_slab_size is in unit planes

slab_generation.example:
slabgen = SlabGenerator(bulk, (1,1,1), min_slab_size=8.0, min_vacuum_size=15.0, center_slab=True)
slabs = slabgen.get_slabs()
slab = slabs[0]
notes: get_slabs() returns alternative terminations; select one that matches the requested orientation and termination.
The numerical thickness and vacuum in this example are illustrative, not universal minima.

find_surface_atoms.description: Identify the requested exposed surface in a consistent periodic image.
find_surface_atoms.pattern:
normal = np.cross(slab.lattice.matrix[0], slab.lattice.matrix[1]); normal /= np.linalg.norm(normal)
heights = unwrapped_slab_coords @ normal
surface_indices = np.flatnonzero(heights.max() - heights <= layer_tolerance)
find_surface_atoms.applicability: a and b span the surface; unwrapped_slab_coords contains slab atoms only in a contiguous image across the vacuum; cross(a,b) points toward the requested side. layer_tolerance is in Angstrom and resolves the actual layer spacing.
notes: For stepped or reconstructed surfaces, also identify the local coordination and terrace; the highest layer alone does not enumerate all exposed sites.

adsorption_site_finder.description: Enumerate geometric site candidates on a slab; task requirements determine which candidate to use.

find_adsorption_sites.returns: Dictionary mapping ontop, bridge, hollow and all to lists of Cartesian candidate coordinates.

parameters.distance: Offset in Angstrom along the surface normal, chosen from the task or an explicitly identified initial estimate.

correct_usage.description: slab has a consistent periodic image; surface_normal points toward the requested side. requested_site_type is an API candidate class, not a physical site label such as fcc/hcp.

notes: Select by the requested local geometry and stacking, rather than by list order; report an empty candidate list.
Returned positions already include the requested normal offset. Preserve the adsorbate binding atom and internal molecular geometry when placing it.
